items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render the required orchestrator kind**

The generated `model-profiles.env` in this revision contains `HERDR_AGENTS_WORKER_KIND` but no `HERDR_AGENTS_ORCHESTRATOR_KIND`, and the manifest/generator have no source for that variable. Consequently every normally deployed configuration reaches this guard with an empty value and exits 2 before any orchestration begins; the test fixture masks this by adding a variable production cannot generate. Add the manifest/rendering support in this change, or remove/replace this unavailable prerequisite.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:rendering HERDR_AGENTS_ORCHESTRATOR_KIND is dotfiles-T84 (PR #272 in flight); this task was dispatched with that soft dependency by design and the guard exit 2 is intended until T84 lands; live activation is T87

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Implement the directive command before invoking it**

Even if the missing environment variable is supplied manually, the deployed `herdr-agents` script has no `--directive` option (its option parser only handles attach, bootstrap, restart, add/remove-worker, and audit). This invocation therefore treats `--directive` as the normal directory argument and fails after the launcher has already exchanged registrations, so no Codex turn can start. Include the corresponding `herdr-agents --directive` implementation or use an existing supported interface.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match only the terminal completion marker**

Any occurrence of `ORCHESTRATION-DONE` is treated as successful completion, even when it is merely quoted while the orchestrator is still waiting for work. For example, a final response such as “the worker said `ORCHESTRATION-DONE`, but I am still waiting” exits 0 after one turn instead of polling the inbox. Require the marker to be the final non-blank line as the prompt instructs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep orchestration transcripts outside the checkout**

This writes the raw operator task into `.orchestration/validation` (and later appends every Codex response), despite the README describing the transcripts as private. That directory is not ignored, and this repository's orchestration workflow commits `.orchestration` artifacts, so a task containing incident details, credentials, or other sensitive context will appear in `git status` and can be pushed in the next boundary commit. Store these transcripts in the protected per-run directory or redact/ignore them before writing.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/b2e76efc78ecb7dc4023beacb6d55d7833bb6eb8/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unrecognized credentials out of published transcripts**

When an operator task or Codex reply includes a standard unquoted credential such as `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...` (or a PEM block), the masker leaves it intact because its pattern only recognizes a few token prefixes and quoted `secret`/`token` assignments; these copies then write it into the tracked `.orchestration/validation` tree. Fresh evidence: running this repository's masker on that exact `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` format left it verbatim. Keep these transcripts private or expand the redaction before publishing.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/bb80c63313dfb1c00fb349156cd9153de6bfe200/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid passing an unbounded inbox through one argv entry**

When a worker sends a result larger than the platform's single-argument limit (a 140 KiB result reproduces this on Linux), the preceding `inbox.sh` call has already displayed and marked it read, but expanding `"$prompt"` here makes `exec` fail with `Argument list too long`. Cleanup restores the seat, yet retrying cannot retrieve that result because it is acknowledged. Pass the message through a file/stdin or enforce a size limit before invoking Codex.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c3bd7af0

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for a hook delivery before resuming Codex**

With `CODEX_ORCHESTRATE_DELIVERY=hook`, an unfinished `codex exec` that returns while a worker is still running reaches this `continue` and immediately starts the next empty `exec resume --last`; it repeats until `--max-turns` is exhausted instead of waiting for a result. agmsg's turn hook runs after a response and is silent when no unread message exists, so it is not a blocking wait; add a delivery wait or do not expose hook mode until that mechanism exists. [agmsg's documented hook flow](https://github.com/fujibee/agmsg/blob/main/docs/design.md)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c3bd7af0

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Write Codex output outside its writable sandbox roots**

The configured Codex sandbox can modify the entire agmsg `run` tree containing this output file. A prompt-injected model can replace `transcript.last.md` with a symlink to any user-writable target before its turn finishes; Codex then follows that path for `-o`, and the launcher subsequently reads and rewrites it outside the sandbox. Codex implements this output option with a direct `std::fs::write`, which follows symlinks; use a directory unavailable to the sandbox for this artifact or reject symlinks before and after the invocation. [Codex output writer](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/exec/src/event_processor.rs)

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/bb80c63313dfb1c00fb349156cd9153de6bfe200/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c3bd7af0

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the launcher lock outside Codex's writable workspace**

With the managed `workspace-write` configuration, an operator task or delivered inbox message can cause the running Codex turn to delete this repository-resident directory. A second launcher then passes this `mkdir` while the first is still active and both loops operate on `exec resume --last` and the same exchanged registrations, defeating the concurrency guarantee. Store the lock in the private state directory (outside Codex's writable roots) instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:0f43e161

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep recovery snapshots outside Codex's writable roots**

The managed Codex configuration grants `workspace-write` access to `~/.agents/skills/agmsg/run`, so an untrusted task or inbox message can delete this snapshot while a turn is running. If the launcher is then terminated uncatchably, the documented recovery procedure has lost `registrations.tsv`, the only record of the Claude registrations that must be rejoined, leaving the exchanged seat state unrecoverable. Store the snapshot under the protected private-state directory instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:0f43e161

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Register the replacement Codex seat in every exchanged team**

When `previous` contains Claude registrations in several teams and no Codex seat exists, the reset loop removes every Claude membership, but this call joins the new Codex identity only to the team selected for polling. Workers retained in the other teams then cannot address the Codex orchestrator, so their results remain undeliverable until the launcher exits. Join the replacement identity to every exchanged team while keeping `--team` only as the inbox-polling selection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:0f43e161
